user.title: Connect your Samsung TV
user.description:
![Connecting your TV](/samstream_files/animations/connect.svg)

Turn the TV on, then enter its IP address. You will be asked to allow the connection on the TV once.

So Home Assistant can also turn the TV **on** (for a doorbell camera at night), switch on Wake-on-LAN on the TV first:
1. **Settings → All Settings → Connection → Network → Expert Settings**.
2. Turn on **Power On with Mobile** (on some models **Power On with Network** or **Wake on LAN**).
3. Optional: **Settings → All Settings → Connection → External Device Manager → Device Connection Manager → Access Notification → First Time Only**, so the TV does not ask again.

A fixed IP for the TV (a DHCP reservation on your router) keeps everything working after restarts.

data_description.host: IP address or hostname of the Samsung TV, for example 192.168.1.11.

pair_failed.description: Make sure the TV is on and you can see it, then select Submit to try again.

reauth_confirm.description: The TV no longer accepts Home Assistant. Stand by the TV, select Submit, then choose Allow on the TV.

reconfigure.title: Change the TV address
reconfigure.description: Enter the new IP address of the same TV.

data_description.host: IP address or hostname of the Samsung TV.

discovery_confirm.title: Add {name}?
discovery_confirm.description: Home Assistant found {name} ({model}) at {host}. Select Submit, then choose **Allow** on the TV.

local_offer.title: Local SmartThings (optional)
local_offer.description:
![Local SmartThings](/samstream_files/animations/connect.svg)

Home Assistant can also control {name} over your own network — its real inputs, picture and sound modes, channel, ambient light and more, with no Samsung account and no internet. The SmartThings app can't control the TV while this is on, and you can switch back any time.

Tick the box to set it up now; Home Assistant guides you (you enter the PIN the TV shows, or run a one-line helper if it can't reach the TV directly).

local_offer_guide.title: Set up local control
local_offer_guide.description:
![Local SmartThings](/samstream_files/animations/connect.svg)

After you select Submit, open **Settings → Devices & services → Samstream → {name} → Configure → Local control** to connect the TV.

If Home Assistant can reach the TV over your network you just enter the 8-digit PIN it shows. If it runs in Docker it usually can't reach the TV directly — on Windows even host mode is on the Docker VM's network, not your LAN — so it will give you a short command to run once on a computer on the TV's network.

progress.wait_for_allow:
![Pairing the TV with Home Assistant](/samstream_files/animations/pairing.svg)

Look at {name}: a message asks whether to allow "Home Assistant Samstream". Choose **Allow** with the remote. Waiting up to 60 seconds.

error.cannot_connect: Cannot reach the TV. Check that it is on and that the IP address is correct.
error.pairing_denied: The TV refused the connection. If you chose Deny by mistake, try again and choose Allow.
error.pairing_timeout: Nobody accepted the request on the TV in time.
error.unknown: Unexpected error, see the Home Assistant log.

abort.wrong_device: That address belongs to a different TV.

network.title: Wake-on-LAN
network.description: Home Assistant wakes the TV with a Wake-on-LAN packet sent to this address. Use your network's broadcast address (for example 192.168.1.255). Inside Docker a global broadcast (255.255.255.255) does not reach the TV.

data_description.wol_target: IPv4 broadcast address of the TV's network, or the TV's own IP.
data_description.extra_apps: Tizen app IDs missing from the built-in list, separated by spaces or commas. Find an app's ID in the current app sensor while it is open.

app_signing.title: App signing
app_signing.description:
Samsung TVs (2023 and newer) only install apps signed with a Samsung certificate made for that TV. Home Assistant creates and keeps one for you.

Current status: **{status}**

menu_options.samsung_sign_in: Sign in with Samsung (helper command, recommended)
menu_options.samsung_paste: Sign in with Samsung (paste from the browser)

samsung_paste.title: Sign in with Samsung
samsung_paste.description:
1. Open this link and sign in with your Samsung account: [Samsung sign-in]({url})
2. Before signing in, open the browser's developer tools (F12) on the **Network** tab.
3. After signing in, the page fails to load *localhost:4794* (expected). Select the **callback** request, open **Payload**, and copy the value of **code**.
4. Paste it below.

data_description.code: The code value from the callback request. It starts with a curly bracket and "access_token" (or with %7B if you chose "view URL-encoded"). You can also paste the whole Payload, state included.

import_certificates.title: Import certificates
import_certificates.description: Use an existing Samsung author and distributor certificate (from Tizen Studio's Certificate Manager or Apps2Samsung). Copy both files into the Home Assistant config folder first. The distributor certificate must list this TV.

data_description.author_p12: Path relative to the config folder, for example samstream/author.p12.
data_description.distributor_p12: Path relative to the config folder, for example samstream/distributor.p12.

tv_app.title: Samstream TV app
tv_app.description: Applied the next time Samstream opens on the TV. Needs the app installed or updated by Home Assistant at least once.

data_description.language: Automatic follows the TV's own language.
data_description.theme: Colors of the home screen; video always plays on black.
data_description.auto_update: When Home Assistant has a newer Samstream TV app (after an integration update), install it by itself the next time the TV is on and Samstream is not on screen.
data_description.resume_playback: When Samstream goes back to the app it interrupted, press Play so it continues. Home Assistant cannot see whether you had paused it with the TV's own remote; turn this off if that leaves apps playing that you had paused. Pauses made through Home Assistant are always kept.
data_description.tv_corner: Where Live TV or the HDMI input stays visible when a camera plays with the TV picture in a corner.
data_description.frame_power: The Frame's Power key switches to Art Mode. Choose Fully off to make 'turn off' (and the camera's return) switch it off completely, like a long press on its remote.

voice_bridge.title: Voice bridge
voice_bridge.description:
Send spoken text to Home Assistant Assist. Anything can POST JSON with a `text` field (for example: turn on the kitchen lights) to this address: a Bixby capsule on your phone, the Samstream TV app, a script. Assist runs it in this TV's area, a `samstream_voice` event fires for your automations, and the answer comes back as `speech`.

Address (keep it secret, anyone with it can talk to Assist):
`{url}`

From outside your home it needs a public address (Home Assistant Cloud or your own).

data.voice_show_reply: Show the answer on this TV

data_description.voice_bridge: Turn off to disable the address; it stays the same when you turn it back on.
data_description.voice_show_reply: Shows what was said and Assist's answer as a short message, only while the TV is on.

local_control.title: Local control (local SmartThings)
local_control.description:
Home Assistant becomes the cloud your TV reports to, over your own network — its real inputs, picture and sound mode, channel, ambient light and more, with no Samsung account and no internet.

A TV works with **either** local control **or** the SmartThings app, never both at once, and you can switch back any time.

Before you start: the TV must be on, Home Assistant must be able to reach it on your network, and the TV must be able to reach Home Assistant on the cloud port (on Docker, publish it: `ports: - "5684:5684"`).

menu_options.local_control_release: Turn off and hand the TV back to SmartThings

local_control_settings.title: Connect the TV
local_control_settings.description:
Home Assistant will run a local cloud on your network for the TV to report to.

The TV will report to `{address}`.
Cloud ID: `{cloud_uuid}`

Keep the access token unless the TV already uses another. The TV must be able to reach this port (on Docker, publish it: `ports: - "5684:5684"`). Next, you'll onboard the TV from a computer on its network.

data_description.ocf_token: The secret the TV presents to Home Assistant. Keep the one shown unless the TV already has another.
data_description.ocf_port: TCP port for every TV (5684 is the standard).
data_description.ocf_host: Leave empty to use Home Assistant's own address on your network.

import_cloud.name: Use an existing local cloud
import_cloud.description: Only if a TV already trusts another local cloud (for example one run from a computer): paste its CA certificate, CA key and cloud ID, so the TV keeps trusting it.

local_control_connect_lan.title: Connect the TV from a computer on its network
local_control_connect_lan.description:
Home Assistant can't reach this TV directly over your network — it runs in Docker, and on Windows even host mode is on the Docker VM's network, not your LAN. So set the TV up from a computer on its own network:

1. On that computer, in a checkout of this project, run:

`{command}`

2. When the TV shows an 8-digit PIN, type it into the tool.
3. The tool prints a credential — paste it below (optional) so Home Assistant can hand the TV back later, then select Submit.

The TV ({tv_ip}) connects on its own; the next screen waits for it.

data_description.credential: Paste what the onboarding tool printed, so Home Assistant can release the TV later. You can leave this empty.

local_control_pin.title: Enter the PIN from the TV
local_control_pin.description:
![Connecting the TV](/samstream_files/animations/pairing.svg)

Look at {name}: it is showing an 8-digit PIN.

Type it below. If no PIN appeared, make sure the TV is on, then try again.

data_description.pin: The 8 digits shown on the TV screen.

local_control_done.title: Paired
local_control_done.description:
![Paired](/samstream_files/animations/paired.svg)

{name} is now connected to Home Assistant over your network. Select Submit to finish.

local_control_trouble.title: The TV did not connect
local_control_trouble.description:
The TV has not reported to Home Assistant yet. The usual reasons:

- **It is still set up in SmartThings** on another phone or account. Remove it there first — a TV answers only one owner.
- **The cloud port is not reachable from Home Assistant.** In Docker, publish it: `ports: - "5684:5684"`.
- **The TV was off overnight**, so it lost the pairing. Turn it on, then try again for a fresh PIN.
- Home Assistant must be on the TV's own network to set it up: on a bridge-networked Docker install it cannot reach the TV over Wi-Fi for onboarding — use host networking.

local_control_release.title: Hand the TV back to SmartThings
local_control_release.description:
Home Assistant will hand the TV back to SmartThings — it keeps its apps and settings and becomes available in the SmartThings app again.

If you pasted the credential during setup, select Submit and Home Assistant releases it. Otherwise run this on the LAN computer, then select Submit:

`uv run python scripts/onboard_tv.py release --tv {tv_ip} --credential <the credential>`

It opens the Samsung sign-in page. Sign in with your Samsung account; this screen continues by itself. The code works once and expires in 10 minutes.

launch_app.name: Launch app
launch_app.description: Opens an app on the TV, or brings it to the front.

app_id.name: App ID
app_id.description: Tizen app ID, for example 111299001912 for YouTube.

close_app.name: Close app
close_app.description: Closes an app; the TV returns to what was on screen before.

app_id.name: App ID
app_id.description: Tizen app ID of the app to close.

install_app.name: Install Samstream app
install_app.description: Installs a signed Samstream .wgt on the TV over Developer Mode (sdb). Returns the TV's install log.

path.name: Package path
path.description: Optional. A .wgt relative to the config folder. Leave empty to install the Samstream app bundled with the integration, signed with Home Assistant's certificates.

play_stream.name: Play camera on TV
play_stream.description: Opens Samstream on the TV and plays a camera (turns the TV on first if needed).

url.name: Stream URL
url.description: RTSP URL to show instead of a camera entity.

label.name: Label
label.description: Name shown on the TV, defaults to the camera name.

message.name: Message
message.description: Text shown over the video, for example who is at the door.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: Go back to what was on the TV after this many seconds. Leave empty to stay until Stop stream.

return_to_previous.name: Return to previous
return_to_previous.description: When the camera ends, reopen the app that was playing and resume it (or turn the TV off again if it was off).

tv_corner.name: TV picture in a corner
tv_corner.description: Keep Live TV, an HDMI input or Home visible in a corner while the camera plays: On uses the corner from the TV app settings. Over a streaming app (YouTube, Netflix) the camera plays normally instead.

show_message.name: Show message on TV
show_message.description: Shows a full-screen message on the TV, optionally with a sound (a chime from the media library or text-to-speech), then returns to what was on.

title.name: Title
title.description: Large heading, for example the room or event.

message.name: Message
message.description: Text under the title; long text scrolls.

severity.name: Severity
severity.description: Colour and icon: info, warning or alert.

sound.name: Sound
sound.description: Audio to play with the message: a media library file or text-to-speech.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: Go back to what was on the TV after this many seconds. Leave empty to stay until Stop stream or Back.

return_to_previous.name: Return to previous
return_to_previous.description: When the message ends, reopen the app that was playing and resume it (or turn the TV off again if it was off).

update_message.name: Update message on TV
update_message.description: Changes the text over the camera, or of the full-screen message, on the TV without reloading it, for example with an AI description that arrives later. Does nothing when Samstream shows neither.

message.name: Message
message.description: New text to show; empty hides the card.

send_keys.name: Press remote keys
send_keys.description: Presses TV remote keys in order, for example KEY_HOME, KEY_DOWN, KEY_ENTER (or just HOME, DOWN, ENTER).

repeats.name: Repeats
repeats.description: How many times to press the whole list.

hold.name: Hold
hold.description: Hold each key this long (0: a normal press).

send_text.name: Type on TV
send_text.description: Types text into the TV's on-screen keyboard (a search box, a login field). Open the field on the TV first.

done.name: Done
done.description: Close the keyboard afterwards, like its Done key.

hold_key.name: Hold key
hold_key.description: Presses a remote key and holds it, for long-press menus or fast seeking.

key.name: Key
key.description: Remote key, for example KEY_ENTER, KEY_RIGHT or ENTER.

pointer.name: Move pointer
pointer.description: Moves the TV's pointer and/or clicks, in apps that show one (the web browser).

stop_stream.name: Return to previous
stop_stream.description: Closes the camera, message or video Samstream shows and goes back to what was on: reopens the app (resuming it if it was playing), or turns the TV off again if Samstream turned it on. Use it with presence or timers.

art_mode.name: Toggle Art Mode
art_mode.description: On a Samsung Frame TV, switches between normal TV and Art Mode (the on-screen artwork). It flips between the two each time and never powers the TV fully off. Choosing which artwork to show is not possible over the local connection on newer Frames; it needs SmartThings.

open_url.name: Open a link
open_url.description: Opens a link on the TV: a YouTube link plays in the YouTube app, any other address opens in the TV's web browser.

url.name: URL
url.description: A YouTube link (watch, youtu.be or Shorts) or any http(s) web address.

developer_mode.title: Developer Mode needed on {name}
developer_mode.description:
![Turning on Developer Mode on the TV](/samstream_files/animations/developer-mode.en.svg)

Home Assistant could not connect to {name} to install the Samstream app. The TV only accepts app installs from the one computer set in its Developer Mode.

The TV's developer host is now **{developer_host}**, and Home Assistant is at **{ha_host}**.

1. On the TV, open **Apps**.
2. Press **1 2 3 4 5** on the remote (or on the on-screen keypad).
3. Turn **Developer mode** on. The Host PC IP has four boxes, one per part: enter **{ha_host_boxes}**, then choose **OK**.
   - TV menu in Arabic or another right-to-left language? The boxes run the other way, so enter the parts reversed: **{ha_host_rtl}** (first box first).
4. Restart the TV: hold the power button until the Samsung logo appears.
5. Run the install again; this message disappears once it works.

If {ha_host} is not this server's address on your network, set the local network URL under **Settings → System → Network**.

If installs still fail after that, Home Assistant checks whether the TV stored the address backwards and tells you.

certificate_expiring.title: Samstream signing certificates expire on {date}
certificate_expiring.description: Home Assistant signs the Samstream TV app with Samsung certificates that last one year. Renew them before {date}: open Samstream → Configure → App signing and sign in with Samsung again. The key stays the same, so the app on your TVs keeps updating.

certificate_expired.title: Samstream signing certificates expired on {date}
certificate_expired.description: Home Assistant can no longer install or update the Samstream TV app. Open Samstream → Configure → App signing and sign in with Samsung again to renew the certificates. The app already on your TVs keeps working.

developer_restart.title: Restart {name} to finish Developer Mode
developer_restart.description:
Developer Mode on {name} is on and points at Home Assistant (**{ha_host}**), but the TV does not accept app installs yet. Samsung TVs start this only after a full restart, once Developer Mode or its host was changed.

1. Hold the power button on the TV's remote until the TV turns off and the Samsung logo appears (a short press only puts it in standby).
2. Wait until the TV has started.
3. Run the install again; this message disappears once it works.

On **The Frame** the power button switches Art Mode instead: unplug the TV (or its One Connect box) for 30 seconds instead. Do the same if holding the button does not help.

If it still fails after a restart, check that nothing blocks port 26101 between this server and the TV.

developer_reversed.title: Developer Mode address is reversed on {name}
developer_reversed.description:
{name} has **{developer_host}** as its Developer Mode host: that is Home Assistant's address **{ha_host}** backwards. Some Samsung TVs mirror the IP field when the menu language is right-to-left (Arabic, Hebrew, Persian), so the numbers are stored in reverse.

Fix it either way:
- **Type it backwards:** in Developer Mode, enter **{developer_host}**, so the TV stores {ha_host}; or
- **Switch the TV to English** (Settings → General → System Manager → Language), set **{ha_host}**, then switch back.

Then restart the TV (hold the power button until the Samsung logo appears) and run the install again.

duid_not_covered.title: Add {name} to your Samsung certificate
duid_not_covered.description:
Home Assistant's Samsung certificate does not list **{name}** (DUID {duid}) yet, so the TV refuses the Samstream app. This happens when the TV was added, or its Developer Mode was not reachable, after you signed in.

1. Open **Settings → Devices & services → Samstream**, then **Configure** on any of your TVs.
2. Choose **App signing → Sign in with Samsung** and sign in as before.
3. Run the install again.

The new certificate covers every Samstream TV Home Assistant knows, and apps already installed keep working.

ocf_port_in_use.title: Local control cannot start
ocf_port_in_use.description: Port {port} is already used on this machine. Choose another port in the Samstream options (Local control), or stop what uses it.

ocf_no_address.title: Local control has no address for the TV
ocf_no_address.description: Home Assistant does not know its own network address. Set it in Settings > System > Network, or enter it in the Samstream options (Local control).

ocf_not_reachable.title: Your TV cannot reach Home Assistant for local control
ocf_not_reachable.description: Home Assistant listens on TCP {port}, but a test connection to it failed. Make sure nothing blocks TCP {port} on this machine.

ocf_not_reachable_container.title: Open port {port} for local control
ocf_not_reachable_container.description: Home Assistant runs in Docker and TCP {port} is not reachable from your network. Add `ports: - "{port}:{port}"` to the Home Assistant service in docker-compose (or use `network_mode: host`; with `docker run`, add `-p {port}:{port}`), then recreate the container. On Docker Desktop also allow TCP {port} in the computer's firewall.

ocf_not_reachable_core.title: Open port {port} for local control
ocf_not_reachable_core.description: TCP {port} is not reachable on this computer. Allow incoming TCP {port} in its firewall.
